definition: Enabling clauses are clauses or provisions in a statute or constitution that gives government officials the authority to put the law into effect and to enforce it. Enabling clauses also can be used as clauses in contracts that give a business entity or individual the authority to carry out part of the contract. While countless pieces of legislation include enabling clauses, some have been particularly famous. Many of the enabling clauses in the Constitution are not only important but also surrounded by arguments over interpretation. A major “enabling clause” exists in international law that allows developing countries to enter into regional trade agreements with terms that would otherwise be disallowed under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).
